_comment: Shapes and Measurements — the CROSS-TRADE core module. It sits beside carpentry rather than inside it, because reading a rule, converting a unit and working out a quantity are the same skills in a joinery shop, a welding bay, an irrigation trench and a dairy room. Built by ../lesson-kit/build.py.
_extraScripts: carpentry.js carries the shared step machinery as well as carpentry's own drawings — a naming seam recorded at the top of shapes.js. carpentry-joints.js is loaded for the drawing registry, `browse` and drawn questions; shapes.js adds the rules, levels, shapes, solids and the findmark/calc/levelread steps.
hubIntro: Reading a measurement, converting between units, working out area and volume, proving a corner square and a surface level, and estimating what a job needs. Every worked example comes from a real trade — none of it is arithmetic for its own sake.
leadsNote: This module serves all six departments. Measurement is the same skill in construction, mechanical engineering, electronics, agriculture, livestock and food processing — only the units and the tolerances change. Where a criterion maps onto the Kenyan Carpentry & Joinery Level 4 units it says so; the other five departments' frameworks are not yet in hand, and a criterion that plainly serves them carries no mapping rather than a guessed one.
endNote: You have measured, calculated and estimated on screen. The measurements that count are taken with a real tape on real work, and checked twice.
